title: Claims-to-Authorization Posting Standard: Unit Use Under Referrals and Authorizations
content:
This posting standard governs how care uses the units of **Referrals and Authorizations**. The units on an authorization are those authorized and not yet used: grants and extensions add units, use consumes them, and cancellation or expiry releases what is left.

## Standard

1. **What one unit is.** One unit is used per the authorization type's definition of one unit used.
2. **When a use is posted.** A use is posted only for a service date inside the validity span of an approved authorization whose servicing provider delivered the service. Whether this holds is read from the authorization's system record: its status, its first and last span days and its servicing provider.
3. **What does not use units.** Services outside the span, or from another provider, consume nothing and are treated as received without authorization.
4. **Exhaustion.** When the units remaining reach zero, the authorization is exhausted on that posting date; further care needs an extension or a new authorization.
5. **Units used.** The units used on an authorization are the total of the units on its use entries over the life of the authorization. Each use entry carries the service date and the claim number and line number of the claim line it comes from.

## Decision table

| Status of the authorization | Service date inside the span | Service delivered by the servicing provider | A use may be posted |
|---|---|---|---|
| approved | yes | yes | yes |
| approved | no | yes | no; treated as received without authorization |
| approved | yes | no | no; treated as received without authorization |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Home Health Care Authorization with a span from 2 March to 30 April has 1 visit remaining. A home visit by the servicing agency on 20 April is posted and brings the units remaining to zero; the authorization is exhausted on that posting date. A visit on 2 May falls outside the span and consumes nothing.
